prompt: Which case normally marks the direct object?
explanation: The accusative case marks the direct object.

explanation: The dative case commonly marks the recipient or beneficiary.

prompt: durch, ohne, gegen, für, um take which case?
explanation: The DOGFU prepositions always take accusative.

prompt: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu take which case?
explanation: These common prepositions always take dative.

prompt: Ich lerne Deutsch, ___ in Berlin zu arbeiten.
explanation: Purpose (“in order to”) is um … zu. um comes first; zu sits right before the infinitive.
hints: This clause states a purpose: in order to work in Berlin.
The pattern is um + rest of the clause + zu + infinitive.

prompt: Ich gehe einkaufen, um Brot ___ kaufen.
explanation: zu comes immediately before the infinitive: um Brot zu kaufen.
hints: um … zu wraps the whole purpose clause.
zu is not at the start; it stands right before kaufen.

prompt: Wir fahren nach Berlin, ___ das Museum zu besuchen.
explanation: um introduces the purpose; zu remains in front of besuchen.

prompt: Ich spare Geld, um ein Auto ___ kaufen.
explanation: Objects stay between um and zu: um ein Auto zu kaufen.
um + (complements) + zu + infinitive expresses purpose: in order to.

prompt: “In order to” with no new subject uses…
explanation: Same subject as the main clause: Ich lerne, um zu arbeiten. A different subject needs damit instead.
With separable verbs, zu slots between prefix and stem: anzurufen, not zu anrufen.

explanation: Ein has no masculine ending: the adjective supplies -er.

explanation: After der in the nominative, the adjective takes -e.
